qs.q: An unimmunized child presents with fever, malaise, and a generalized vesicular rash that appears in successive crops, showing lesions in various stages of healing from papules to crusts. What is the definitive diagnostic method to differentiate this from smallpox?
o: Viral culture on human embryonic fibroblast monolayers observing characteristic plaque formation.
Tzanck smear examination of scrapings from the base of vesicles to identify cells.
Direct fluorescent antibody staining of skin scrapings using monoclonal anti-variola.
Electron microscopy visualization of brick-shaped virions in crust samples from lesions.
Polymerase chain reaction amplification of vesicular fluid targeting viral DNA sequences.
qs.e: PCR is the gold standard and most sensitive method to definitively differentiate VZV from smallpox and other rash illnesses.
